Incorporating Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey insights (July 2020), the tone skews more negative than the FSR-adjusted view. Banks reported widespread tightening of lending standards and terms for C&I loans to firms of all sizes and for CRE loans, along with weaker business loan demand; consumer credit (credit cards, auto) also saw broad tightening and softer demand. While low rates boosted demand for residential mortgages, banks still tightened mortgage standards and HELOC demand fell. Many banks expected further tightening amid pandemic-related uncertainty. These SLOOS findings suggest a restrictive bank credit channel that could constrain the recovery even as FOMC policy support (near-zero rates, continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, repo and RRP operations) keeps market functioning orderly. Net: persistent virus-related risks plus tighter bank intermediation imply a more negative balance of risks than indicated by FSR alone.
